title: objectql: a system-context write skips the reference check on every lookup/user field, and no key keeps it on — a runAs system flow stores an owner that resolves to no account
body:
Filed by the objectstack-ai/duly lane seat from a measurement on duly (objectstack-ai/duly#148, PR objectstack-ai/duly#158). For central triage; no `domain:*` label is set here.

## What happens

`assertReferencesResolve` (`engine-referential-integrity.ts`) opens with `if (context?.isSystem) return;`. `service-automation`'s `resolveRunDataContext` gives every `runAs: 'system'` flow run `isSystem: true`. So `create_record` / `update_record` in an elevated flow store a reference to a deleted row with no error, while the same write on the user path is refused with `reference_not_found`.

The integrity audit names this exemption itself: "a system-context write is exempt from the write-time reference check, so this audit is where such a reference surfaces".

An elevated flow needs elevation for **authorization**, to write rows owned by other people. It does not need it to store dangling ids, but the two are bundled. No authorable key separates them: `CreateRecordConfigSchema` is strict (`objectName` / `fields` / `outputVariable`), there is no per-node `runAs`, and there is no field-level key.

## Measurement

On duly `main` `25743ed`, @objectstack 18.2.0, booted kernel, SQLite:

- A user-path `data.insert('duly_task', …)` naming a deleted `sys_user` id is refused with `Owner: no sys_user record has id …`.
- The same insert with `isSystem` is created.
- `duly_assignment_fanout` (`runAs: 'system'`) over [live, deleted, banned] gives `acted: 3`, 3 tasks and 0 errors.

Also: deleting the `sys_user` row left its id in `duly_assignment.assignees`, a multi-user field that is not cleaned up.

The same early return is on objectstack `main` at `69c9f7c6`.

## Ask

A way for an elevated write to keep the reference check while keeping its authorization elevation. That could be the default for `create_record` / `update_record` under `runAs: 'system'`, or an opt-in key. Triage decides which.

The app-side workaround is duly PR #158: a guard in the flow, labelled as such. It is removed when the platform ships this.
